reasons: Classification is correct: the original Section 15 requires unqualified prior written approval for Customer assignment with only an affiliate carve-out and no successor/M&A carve-out, so it fails the fallback ('mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent not unreasonably withheld') on two material terms and approaches the walk-away position.

The redline is actionable and directionally correct: it adds the affiliate/successor carve-out for Client, imposes a 'not unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed' standard, and bars TrueLink from transferring to a Client competitor — all squarely within the preferred position; it is grammatically coherent and leaves the mutual structure intact.
The rationale correctly confirms no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right exists elsewhere, so no deletion operation is needed for that limb.

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.67 changed-character ratio) is explained by the rule genuinely requiring insertion of the consent standard, the M&A carve-out and the competitor bar into a single-sentence clause; it is not evidence of over-editing.

Minor, non-fatal: narrowing the previously mutual affiliate carve-out to Client only (consistent with the preferred position that Vendor may not assign without consent) is not disclosed in the comment — worth adding a clause to the note so the change in Vendor's rights is transparent.
